known: shape reads chunks via cached_cumsum, identity-keyed lru_cache

root_causes.description: Derived shape is recomputed through a wrapper and cache lookup on every access.

findings.problem: Array.shape recomputes per access: wrapper allocation and lru_cache lookup with Python-level hash and eq per dimension; result not stored.
findings.performance_principle: Do not recompute a value derived from immutable state on every read.

evidence.statement: shape property is uncached and calls cached_cumsum per dimension; identity-keyed lru_cache means steady-state cost is constant, with no runtime evidence.

findings.conditions: Matters only if .shape is read very many times, or many distinct chunk tuples exceed the default 128-entry lru_cache.

counter_evidence.statement: Identity-keyed caching already avoids value hashing; no super-linear cost found.

findings.recommendation: Store the computed shape per chunk assignment or use sum(c) for the last element, avoiding the cumsum tuple and cache lookup.
findings.trade_offs: A stored shape needs invalidation when _chunks is reassigned.

validation.falsifier: no measurable change on the supplied workload
